validity.recommendation: Owner shares need a ruling: the sheet lists the Ukrainian operator at 100 percent beside Gazprom and QazaqGaz.
validity.researcher_notes: Soyuz is a real line. Russian Wikipedia, the Russian dispatch directorate and Intergas Central Asia all describe the Orenburg to Uzhhorod export trunk through Kazakhstan and Ukraine, so it exists and is correctly a gas transmission trunk. It is not a duplicate of any other Ukraine row: it shares a corridor with P0768 and P0774 but is a separate string. Length 2750 km is the whole line, and 1568 km of it is in Ukraine. Capacity 25.2 matches the dispatch directorate, while Russian Wikipedia gives 26 bcm/y design and English Wikipedia 26.1 for the Ukrainian section. Owner1 at 100 percent beside two other owners is a notation question for Baird. No page found states ownership shares.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Mothballed still fits. A Neftegaz report from 11 May 2022 describes the Ukrainian operator shutting the Sokhranivka station, the only entry point of Soyuz from Russia. Russian transit through Ukraine ended on 1 January 2025 when the agreement between the Ukrainian operator and Gazprom expired. Ukraine imported 6.5 bcm of gas in 2025, mostly from Hungary and Poland, so the Ukrainian system is in use, but no page found names this line as carrying that gas. This evidence covers the Ukrainian section. The Russian and Kazakh sections were not checked.
